questions.question: Differentiate between the Four-Point and Ten-Point Systems of fabric inspection.
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between the Four-Point and Ten-Point Systems of fabric inspection.
  •  4 - POINT SYSTEM
  • The 4-Point System is a widely used method for evaluating and grading fabric quality based on the size of
  • defects. It is commonly used in garment and textile industries for both supplier inspection and incoming fabric
  • inspection.
  • The Main Principle is bigger the defect, the higher the penalty points.
  • A single defect is assigned a maximum of 4 penalty points based on its size.
  • Point Allocation
  • Size of defect Points
  • Up to 3 inches 1 point
  • Over 3 – 6 inches 2 points
  • Over 6 – 9 inches 3 points
  • Over 9 inches 4 points
  • /
  •  10 - POINT SYSTEM
  • The 10-Point System is a traditional method of evaluating and grading fabric quality based on the size and
  • severity of fabric defects. It is mainly used for inspecting and grading woven fabrics, particularly in textile and
  • garment industries.
  • The Main Principle is that larger defects are given higher penalty points because they have a greater effect
  • on fabric quality.
  • A defect is assigned penalty points according to its length/size, with a maximum of 10 points for a single
  • defect.
  • Point Allocation
  • Size of defect Points
  • Up to 1 inch 1 point
  • Over 1 – 5 inches 3 points
  • Over 5 – 10 inches 5 points
  • Over 10 inches 10 points
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: Over 10 inches 10 points

questions.question: Explain the steps involved in payment through a documentary LC.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the steps involved in payment through a documentary LC.
  • A Letter of Credit (L/C) is a payment method in which the buyer’s bank guarantees payment to the exporter
  • when the exporter fulfil the conditions mentioned in the L/C and submits the required documents.
  • In garment exports, the buyer opens the L/C through their bank, and the exporter manufactures and ships
  • the garments. After shipment, the exporter submits documents such as the commercial invoice, packing list,
  • and Bill of Lading to the bank. The bank checks the documents and makes payment according to the L/C
  • terms.
  • L/C may be Sight L/C, where payment is made immediately after document verification, or Usance L/C,
  • where payment is made after an agreed period.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: where payment is made after an agreed period.

questions.question: Explain the complete process of fabric sourcing in garment manufacturing.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the complete process of fabric sourcing in garment manufacturing.
  • SOURCING OF FABRICS
  • Fabric sourcing refers to the process of identifying, evaluating and selecting suitable fabric suppliers
  • according to the requirements of a particular garment order.
  • The objective of fabric sourcing is to obtain the right fabric in the required quality, quantity, price and delivery
  • period.
  • The sourcing team looks for fabrics that meet the buyer's requirements for:
  • • Fabric type – cotton, polyester, denim, linen, viscose, etc.
  • • Fabric construction – woven or knitted.
  • • Weight/GSM – how heavy or light the fabric is.
  • • Colour and shade – matching the buyer's approved colour.
  • /
  • • Composition – e.g., 100% cotton or 60% cotton + 40% polyester. Etc…
  • TYPES OF SOURCING
  • Local sourcing → Supplier is within the country.
  • Global sourcing → Supplier is in another country.
  • Direct sourcing → Buyer deals directly with the manufacturer.
  • Indirect sourcing → An intermediary is involved.
  • Online Sourcing → Sourcing and Check availability of fabric through online.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: Online Sourcing → Sourcing and Check availability of fabric through online.

• Compare sea shipment and air shipment with respect to cost, speed, capacity, suitability and
  • reliability.
  •  Sea Transportation
  • Transportation of goods through ships and cargo vessels across seas and oceans.
  • Advantages
  • • Suitable for large quantities
  • • Lower cost per unit for international bulk shipments
  • • Suitable for containerized garment exports
  • • Ideal for long-distance international transportation
  • Disadvantages
  • • Slow compared with air transportation
  • • Dependent on port schedules
  •  Air Transportation
  • Transportation of goods using cargo aircraft or commercial aircraft cargo services.
  • Advantages
  • • Very fast
  • • Suitable for urgent shipments
  • • Long international distances can be covered quickly
  • Disadvantages
  • • Very expensive
  • • Limited cargo capacity compared with ships
